risks.note: ALMM List I enlisted module capacity of 173.14 GW as at March 2026 against annual domestic installation demand of approximately 44 GW is stated to create intense pricing competition in non-DCR segments. This is the single most structural threat to SHPV's module economics. Mitigation claimed: competing on quality, certification breadth and compliance, delivering TOPCon modules at near-market pricing, and using ALMM compliance to stay eligible for DCR schemes where competitive dynamics are 'structurally moderated'; separately, 40-50% of modules produced are intended to be consumed by SWELECT's own EPC/IPP businesses.
risks.risk: Domestic module overcapacity and competitive pricing pressure

risks.note: Frequent changes in ALMM, net metering, open access banking or Basic Customs Duty structures disrupt planning and project economics. Mitigation: proactive MNRE/NSEFI engagement, compliance monitoring, regulatory-change provisions written into long-term contracts, and a diversified revenue base reducing single-category concentration. Materially relevant because eligibility for PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM, CPSU Phase-II and SECI tenders rests entirely on ALMM/DCR listing.

Global conflicts and trade policy uncertainty create input cost volatility and logistics disruption; specifically, antidumping and countervailing duty investigations initiated by the United States in August 2025 introduced near-term uncertainty for Indian exporters and prompted a stated reorientation toward Europe, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. Mitigation claimed: predominantly domestic revenue, long-term fixed-price PPA revenues from IPP, secured cell supply through structured long-term partnerships, and a diversified model spanning manufacturing, EPC, IPP, BESS and channels.
risks.risk: Geopolitical and supply chain risk, including US trade action

risks.note: SHPV is a module assembler that does not make its own cells - it sources cells from Tier-1 suppliers through structured long-term partnerships, with strategic buffer inventory as an additional layer. Management asserts supply continuity and pricing are assured and that domestically manufactured cell supply is assured, but the dependence itself is structural and is called out by the Company as its own named risk category.

Rapid advancement in solar technology demands continuous investment to stay competitive. Mitigation: upward-compatible manufacturing lines, a TOPCon-first strategy aligned with the dominant technology cycle through 2028-2030, PVEL certification enrolment (completion expected FY 2026-27) and an expanding R&D programme. The stated 2028-2030 horizon is itself an implicit obsolescence deadline for the 2 GW line.

FY 2025-26 was SWELECT's formal entry into BESS as a structured commercial vertical, introducing technology and execution risk in a segment where revenue is still prospective (residential awaiting BIS CRS certification, C&I at pilot stage, utility scale at tender stage). Mitigation: phased approach from the operational 500 kW Wind-Solar-BESS pilot, structured technology partnerships with established OEMs, and careful due diligence on battery supply, backed by four decades of power-electronics heritage.

Scaling manufacturing, EPC and IPP simultaneously elevates working capital needs. Mitigation: project finance in place for all IPP projects, financial closure targeted at the start of execution to cut construction-stage requirements, optimised and enhanced bank working-capital lines, and liens freed on fixed deposits and mutual funds to release equity for new IPP projects. Note that this last item implies previously encumbered liquid assets.
risks.risk: Working capital intensity from scaling three capital-hungry businesses at once

risks.note: Sector-wide talent shortages and wage inflation threaten operational continuity and execution. Mitigation: SESL cites a committed workforce with average tenure of 11+ years; SHPV relies on localised hiring, structured in-house training, campus recruitment partnerships and retention programmes including a women's workforce initiative targeting growth from 31% to 50% of core production roles, which also widens the hiring pool.
risks.risk: Human resource risk - talent shortage and wage inflation
